newsitem.title: UK: Palladium, platinum soar on S.African strike.
newsitem.headline: Palladium, platinum soar on S.African strike.

text.p: Platinum and palladium prices soared to fresh highs on Wednesday on news of an illegal strike in South Africa, the world's largest platinum producer.
Palladium, platinum's sister metal, surged to a high of $188.00 per ounce compared to a fixing on Tuesday afternoon of $177.50.
"The market has gone crazy. The market is very, very tight," said a dealer.
About 15 to 20 percent of production has been affected since workers at Anglo American Platinum Corp's Rustenburg operation went on a wildcat strike on Tuesday.
Platinum prices broke through the $400 mark, hitting a peak of $404 in early activity.
The strike comes against a backdrop of supply shortages which have been strangling the market since Russia, the biggest producer of palladium, halted shipments last December.

Platinum prices were the highest since May 1996 and palladium has surpassed a peak set in 1989, a dealer said. It was unclear when palladium prices were this high since his records did not go back that far, he added.
